title: The West Village home and the wedding at No. 2 Bank Street
summary: Gil and Anita describe living in the Village, being married by a minister they found in the phone book, and their rings.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: We've lived in this neighborhood all this time. The children were born on 15th Street.
Oh really? Where?
We've been here five years in a brownstone and we bounced all on 15th Street, what was the address, 125?
Where were you married and under what circumstances?
The West Village. We never got out of the village.
Well, I meant at home or were you married in a church?
It was in an apartment. We looked up a minister in the phone books.
Yes, we thought we could find one within walking distance. (LAUGHTER).
On No. 2 Bank Street. And it turned out to be a peculiar coincidence. He was 75, he was 76 and his wife was 55. It was like the same kind of difference between our ages.
Between the two of you. Well I must tell you at a time I might have been aghast at that but as I said, I've learned so much about old men I am no longer aghast. (LAUGHTER). Do you remember his name?
He gave us a ......
A certificate?
An all-American kind of Presbyterian name.
And he said we've got to have a whole lot of happiness, you know. That kind of Spanish. There he was, with all his kids around. They were attendants.
That's right, the children were .........
And who was your first wife? Do you want to say a little bit about that?
It was funny, I said how much do I owe you? And he said, well whatever you think your wife is worth, put that one on me, right? (LAUGHTER). I think I gave him ten, because it's all I could afford.
None of that two dollar stuff.
Yes, it's been a long time story huh? Well now, did you, that looks as though it might be a later style wedding ring. Is that the one you actually married with?
No, we got these in a little jewelery store next to the Vanguard. What did we have at first, plain ones didn't we?
Yes plain. They were round gold ones.
Plain round gold ones, yes.
Yes, but this wasn't expensive, they are much more jolly.
Yes, yes.
( ?) scope and his is like musical bars.
This was twenty-five dollars, but it's cute.
